market_holds: Spot $77.54 at the 18:08 UTC seal (sealed baseline), 1.5% off the 52-week low and 52% below the high. Down 5.3% over 5 sessions and 3.2% over 20. Front-expiry (11-20) straddle 7.28%, event-implied move 6.57%, 25d skew +1.2 vol points, put/call OI 0.62, so the options lean is balanced. Short interest 12.2m shares, about 3.6% of float, 6 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30, per the sweep row). Consensus (Zacks, published 2026-11-12): revenue $4.61B, about RMB31.3B at the 6.78 rate Baidu used in Q2, so roughly flat on Q3 2025's RMB31.2B and on Q2 2026's RMB31.3B. Non-GAAP EPS $0.85 against $1.06 in Q2, after a 40.1% downward revision in the last 30 days, so the estimates are fresh and already cut. The company gives no numeric guidance. In August management said ad pressure would continue through H2 and AI Cloud Infra would keep growing strongly. The story the stock trades on: online marketing fell 19% YoY to RMB13.1B in Q2, while AI Cloud Infra grew 50% to RMB7.3B but fell 17% QoQ. Q2 (2026-08-18) gapped -9.4% and closed -12.7% on a revenue miss and a 68% fall in net income, and Morgan Stanley went to Underweight with an $80 target, which the stock is now below. Earlier reactions by my own arithmetic from Yahoo bars: Nov 2025 open -4.1% / close +2.7%, Feb 2026 open -2.6% / close -5.7%, May 2026 open about +5.8% / close +1.8%. The baseline's 6-K history (median 0.7%) is buyback and monthly-return filings, not earnings, and I did not use it.
view: This is a name the market has already derated hard. It sits below the most bearish broker target, it has outperformed KWEB slightly over the last week (-5% against -8%), and the sell side has just cut EPS 40%. Market cap is about $27B against $41.7B of cash and investments (Q2 release). Nothing I found since the Q2 call changes the two lines this print turns on. On ads: QuestMobile's September data, as reported, shows Baidu's group de-duplicated users down 1.8% YoY while Doubao leads AI apps at 419m MAU. That points to continued erosion, which is consistent with what management guided and what consensus models. My own arithmetic gives about RMB12.4B for Q3 ads if the 2025 Q2-to-Q3 seasonality repeats, roughly -19% YoY, with no sign of an inflection either way. On AI Cloud Infra: the Q2 base was lumpy (Q1 RMB8.8B, Q2 RMB7.3B) and 2025 was restated, so I cannot rebuild the YoY growth with confidence. The bar is low and fresh, which takes away the stale-estimate gap in either direction. HK buybacks of about 550k shares a day ran through September and then paused for the pre-results blackout. They are known and should resume after the print, which is mild support beyond the window rather than a surprise. The China tech tape was weak into the weekend (BABA -7% on 11-12). There is no Kunlunxin IPO filing, hearing or Stock Connect confirmation inside the window that I could find. I see no line where the evidence makes one side clearly more likely than the price assumes. The low bar and depressed valuation tilt it slightly up, and continued ad erosion plus a weak sector tape tilt it slightly down.

recommendation.reason: I found no dated evidence that puts the deciding lines (ad decline rate, AI Cloud Infra growth, margin) on one side of what consensus assumes. The estimates were cut 40% in the last 30 days, so the bar is fresh rather than stale. Sentiment and valuation are already at their lows, and the remaining upside skew is not strong enough to bet on.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Online marketing revenue declining at clearly under 15% YoY with AI Cloud Infra re-accelerating QoQ (long). Or ads at 20% or worse with another sequential drop in AI Cloud Infra (short).

self_critique: The case for long: consensus EPS was slashed 40% in a month and the stock trades below the most bearish target and far below net cash and investments. With buybacks set to resume, even a merely in-line print could trigger a relief rally like May's +5.8% open, so 52 may understate the skew. The case for short: ad erosion is structural, AI Cloud Infra already fell sequentially once, and heavier AI spending (the likely reason for the EPS cut) could again come in worse than modelled, as in August. Neither case rests on evidence the price does not hold, so I stay close to 50.
approach_notes: P4 and P6 helped most: checking the age of the revision showed the bar was fresh, and taking the run-in apart showed it was the tape. The sweep's 'already in the wire' link was a 2025 article, and many search hits were prior-cycle Baidu pieces, so verifying dates took a large share of the time.
